structure.summary: Multi-turn. Each assistant message carries exactly one question card, then waits; each later message opens with a one-line [✓] echo of the last answer before the next card. After the last answer comes a stacked resolved view and a one-sentence confirmation request; after confirmation, a short implication paragraph and then the work.

elements.description: Question card inside a fenced code block: box-drawn header (┌─┐│└┘) whose top border carries a lowercase `quiz · NN/NN` counter, a `[?]` question line, an optional `why it matters:` line, the options, and a `// reply:` hint as the last line.
Options as `A · short-label` lines, each followed by one fluid sentence (what it does, why it fits, how it plays out), two-space indent with hanging-indent wraps.
A one-sentence plain-prose reply hint on the line after the card, outside the code block.
After each user reply: a one-line `[✓] NN label → X · choice` echo (with any note), followed in the same message by the next card.
After the last reply: the full resolved view, one `[✓]` line per question stacked, then a one-sentence confirmation request.
After confirmation: a short paragraph restating the implication (what will be done, skipped, and how), then the work begins.

rubric.criterion: Every question card is a fenced code block with a box-drawn header whose top border carries a lowercase `quiz · NN/NN` counter, a `[?]` question line, and a `// reply:` hint as its last line.
rubric.pass: All cards have the code block, box-drawn header, lowercase `quiz · NN/NN` counter in the top border, `[?]` line and closing `// reply:` hint.
rubric.partial: Cards are code blocks with a box header, but in at least one card the counter, `[?]` marker or `// reply:` hint is missing or malformed.
rubric.source: The look → The question card; Rules of the look #1-3, #7

rubric.criterion: Options are lettered `A · short-label` lines, each with one sentence saying what the option does, why it fits this request, and its practical cost or benefit.
rubric.pass: Every option on every card has the `X · label` form and a single sentence covering what, why and the concrete cost or benefit.
rubric.partial: Label form is right, but some option sentences are fragments, list-like, or skip the why or the cost/benefit.

rubric.criterion: The turn rhythm holds: each card is followed by a one-sentence prose reply hint, and each answer is echoed as a one-line `[✓]` confirmation that opens the message carrying the next card.
rubric.pass: Every card has the prose hint after it, and every answered question gets its one-line `[✓]` echo at the top of the next message, followed by the next card.
rubric.partial: The rhythm mostly holds but at least one prose hint or `[✓]` echo is missing, or an echo sits in a message of its own.
rubric.source: The look → The rhythm; Flow steps 3 and 5

rubric.criterion: After the last answer the skill shows a resolved view with one `[✓]` line per question and asks for confirmation in one sentence; once confirmed, it restates the implication in one short paragraph before doing the work.
rubric.pass: Resolved view lists every question as a `[✓]` line, a one-sentence confirmation ask follows, and after confirmation a short implication paragraph precedes the work.
rubric.partial: The ending is there but incomplete: a question missing from the resolved view, a multi-sentence ask, or no implication paragraph.

rubric.criterion: No assistant message contains more than one question card.
rubric.pass: Every message has at most one card.
rubric.partial: Never applies: two cards in one message is a miss.
rubric.source: Rules of the look #8; What NOT to do

rubric.criterion: Each card marks exactly one option `(recommended)` and that option's sentence names the specific reason it fits this request.
rubric.pass: Every card has exactly one `(recommended)` with a reason tied to the request (or no tag on a card that is a genuine toss-up).
rubric.partial: Tags are present but at least one card's reason is generic, or one card has two tags or an unexplained tag.

rubric.criterion: The quiz asks no more than about seven questions, and the counter's total stays the same and matches the number actually asked.
rubric.pass: Seven or fewer questions (or an offer to switch to /squiz for more), and the `NN/NN` total is constant and equals the questions asked.
rubric.partial: Within the cap but the counter's total changes mid-quiz or ends up not matching.
rubric.source: Rules of the look #9; The look → counter

rubric.criterion: Each `[✓]` echo records what the user actually replied: the letter and any note, the recommended option for a skip or 'you decide', or the closest option for free prose.
rubric.pass: Every echo matches the reply it confirms, notes included.
rubric.partial: One echo drops a note or maps a free-prose or deferred reply to a debatable option.

rubric.criterion: Cards contain no markdown bold or italics, no tables, and no emojis outside sample content.
rubric.pass: No bold/italic markup, tables or decorative emojis inside any card.
rubric.source: Rules of the look #10; What NOT to do

rubric.criterion: The questions asked are the ones whose answers would materially change the work for this request, most load-bearing first, and none re-asks something the prompt already settled.
rubric.pass: Every question would change the resulting work, the first is the biggest decision, and nothing already stated in the prompt is asked again.
rubric.partial: Mostly right, but one question is filler, redundant with the prompt, or clearly out of order.

rubric.criterion: Each card's options are realistic, distinct choices for this request, and the recommendation is the sensible default given what the user said.
rubric.pass: On every card the options are genuinely different, plausible for this request, and the recommendation fits the stated context.
rubric.partial: One card has overlapping or strawman options, or a recommendation that ignores something the user said.

rubric.criterion: The implication paragraph and the work that follows reflect every resolved answer and note, so the user gets what they chose.
rubric.pass: Every answer and note visibly shapes the implication paragraph and the delivered work; nothing chosen is dropped or contradicted.
rubric.partial: One answer or note is missing from, or softened in, the implication or the work.
rubric.appliesWhen: the run reaches confirmation and the skill begins the work
